stories.headline: Two die as cyclone Murasu hits Andhra Pradesh, educational centres shut
stories.title: Two die as cyclone Murasu hits Andhra Pradesh, educational centres shut
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
article_sentences: Odisha and Andhra Pradesh declared holidays for educational institutions in several districts and continued evacuations as Cyclone Murasu battered parts of the two states.
The storm weakened into a cyclonic storm on Tuesday afternoon as it moved over South Coastal Andhra Pradesh.

Murasu moved north-northwestwards at 7 kmph in the six hours up to 2.30 pm and weakened into a cyclonic storm over the same region, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in an official release.

“Severe cyclonic storm Murasu weakened into a cyclonic storm over South Coastal Andhra Pradesh,” it said, adding that the weather system was located 40 km west-northwest of Bapatla, 60 km north of Ongole and 80 km southwest of Vijayawada.
The maximum sustained wind speed was 80-90 kmph, gusting up to 100 kmph at 2.30 pm.

“The cyclonic storm is very likely to continue to move north-northwestwards and weaken into a deep depression (wind speed reaching 55-65 kmph (and) gusting to 75 kmph) by midnight of today,” the weather department said.
At least two people died in cyclone-related incidents in Andhra Pradesh, an official said on Tuesday.
Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) Managing Director Prakhar Jain said 12,230 people were being sheltered in rehabilitation centres.
Preliminary estimates put the damage at Rs 344 crore, with standing crops over 52,459 hectares damaged by heavy rain.
A total of 312 houses were damaged, while the government was actively monitoring 814 minor irrigation tanks and had placed 776 on high alert, Jain added.
Rain battered parts of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
In Andhra Pradesh, where the cyclone made landfall, heavy rain was reported in Prakasam, Nellore, Bapatla and NTR districts as the storm moved inland.

stories.headline: Assam: Dikhow River Erosion Threatens 8 Villages with Flood Disaster
stories.title: Assam: Dikhow River Erosion Threatens 8 Villages with Flood Disaster
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: NAZIRA: Severe erosion has affected a portion of the embankment along the Dikhow river near Houkajan Satra at Mathiachiga in Nazira, triggering serious concern among residents over the threat of a major flood disaster.
Following the devastating flood of the Dikhow river on July 19, a substantial portion of the embankment in front of the residence of a resident, Bijit Mahanta, was washed away by the strong current.

Residents fear that if the damaged section is not repaired before the next monsoon season, several villages, including Houkajan Satra, Bhakat Gaon, Mathiachiga, Dihingia Gaon, Mechagarh, Naosalia, Jaysagar, and Rajmao, could face severe flooding.
The damaged embankment has also disrupted road connectivity, causing immense hardship to residents, students, and patients who depend on the route for transportation.
Although villagers have levelled the eroded portion with soil to facilitate the movement of students, the road remains unsuitable even for small vehicles.

According to residents, they had already informed Nazira MLA Mayur Borgohain and the Executive Engineer of the Water Resources Department about the alarming situation and requested immediate intervention.
However, they alleged that neither the MLA nor senior departmental officials had visited the affected site so far to assess the extent of the damage.

stories.title: Gold, silver rebound: US election impact, India's demand and buying trends explained
stories.summary: Gold and silver prices recovered in international markets on Wednesday, rebounding from sharp losses driven by crude oil trends, US monetary policy expectations, and geopolitical developments.

article_sentences: Gold and silver prices recovered in international markets on Wednesday, rebounding from sharp losses driven by crude oil trends, US monetary policy expectations, and geopolitical developments.
Gold and silver prices recovered in international markets on Wednesday, November 4, after declining sharply in the previous session.
Softer crude oil prices, expectations around US monetary policy and developments in the ongoing geopolitical conflicts remain key factors influencing bullion prices.
On the COMEX, gold futures were trading at $3,963.20 per ounce, up $22.80 or 0.58% from the previous close of $3,940.80 an ounce.
Prices touched a high of $3,970.20 and a low of $3,928.20 an ounce.
COMEX silver futures gained 0.48% to $49.990 per ounce, against the previous close of $49.825 an ounce.
The metal traded between $49.405 and $50.205 anounce.
In the spot market, gold rose 0.2% to $3,934.75 per ounce, while silver slipped 0.2% to $49.67 per ounce in early Asian trade.
The recovery follows a decline in domestic bullion prices on Tuesday (November 3).
In Delhi, gold of 99.9% purity fell ₹700 to ₹1.41 lakh per 10 grams, while silver declined ₹2,000 to ₹1.84 lakh per kg, according to the All India Sarafa Association.
Why are gold and silver prices moving?
Softer crude oil prices: Oil prices fell around 1% on Tuesday (November 3) to their lowest level in nearly four weeks.

stories.title: Nasdaq futures slump over 500 points after midterm election trends point to Democrat sweep
stories.summary: CNBC's election desk projects that the control of the US House "leans Democratic" and that Democrats will win a minimum of over 200 seats from the Chambers 435, while Republicans could win at least 160.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: CNBC's election desk projects that the control of the US House "leans Democratic" and that Democrats will win a minimum of over 200 seats from the Chambers 435, while Republicans could win at least 160.

Futures on Wall Street have sharply reversed course on Wednesday, November 4, as early trends from the midterm election results are pointing towards the Democrats gaining control of the House of Representatives, and leading in the Senate race as well.
Nasdaq futures, which at one point, were up 200 points, buoyed by results from chipmaker AMD, reversed course to fall as much as 500 points.
Even the Dow Futures, which at one point, were trading near the flat line, are now trading with losses of close to 150 points.
Analysts at Deutsche Bank and Societe Generale have warned that a Democrat sweep of both the House and Senate will certainly pressure the AI infrastructure buildout.

Benchmark indices on Wall Street ended mixed on Tuesday, November 3, while the Nasdaq futures have edged higher in post-market trading ahead of the midterm election results outcome, which will be declared in a few hours from now.
The Dow Jones ended Tuesday's session with losses of close to 200 points, reversing most of Monday's gains.
The S&P 500 gained 0.4%, Nasdaq Composite gained 0.8%, while the Nasdaq 100 index ended 0.7% higher, but remained in "correction territory."
Why Are The Nasdaq Futures Surging?
Nasdaq 100's futures though, are trading with gains of close to 200 points after strong results, and an equally strong, if not better commentary from AMD and its MD & CEO Lisa Su.
The stock is up 8% in extended trading after its third quarter results beat street expectations, as did the company's guidance for the fourth quarter.
The surge in AMD's shares in afterhours trade comes after the stock had snapped a three-day losing streak during Tuesday's regular session, ending nearly 4% higher.

stories.headline: Election Commission completes Form 6 U-turn, drops SIR para a Commissioner called ‘illegal’
stories.title: Election Commission completes Form 6 U-turn, drops SIR para a Commissioner called ‘illegal’
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: IN THE latest of a series of U-turns that have effectively undone almost every decision the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had objected to in 14 notes over 10 months, the Election Commission of India (ECI) has now taken the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) declaration out of the online version of the statutory voter enrolment form, Form 6, on its ECINet portal in the states where the SIR is still under way.
What this means is that the declaration inserted between Sections J and K of the online enrolment application for new voters is no longer part of Form 6.

This declaration asked applicants to choose one of three statements: whether their name appeared in the electoral roll during the last SIR held in the early 2000s, whether the name of a parent or grandparent appeared in that roll, or whether neither their name nor that of their parents appeared in it.
An applicant could not proceed without answering it.
Joshi had written on May 16 that no such change could be made without a legal amendment to the form.
Sandhu, on August 13, called it “unauthorised/illegal”.
This declaration is now available on the portal as a separate form.
The development comes after the Commission told the Supreme Court, in its counter-affidavit filed on October 26, that its ER (Electoral Roll) Division had decided on October 21 to split the two.

The affidavit says the SIR-related declaration had been placed inside Form 6 so that an applicant would generate a single OTP and a single e-signature rather than two, and that this “bonafide objective became a subject matter of deliberation and suggestions”.
It goes on to state, “It has been decided vide decision dt.

21.10.2026 of the ER Division that as in the case of submitting the Application in Form 6 in a physical format, the online Application shall also be in two parts i.e. Form 6 as prescribed in the Rules and the SIR Declaration.”
This is the third position the Commission has taken on Form 6 in six weeks, and it completes a reversal.

stories.headline: Rajiv-Farooq rigged 1987 polls: Ram Madhav
stories.title: Rajiv-Farooq rigged 1987 polls: Ram Madhav
stories.summary: Jammu, Nov 3: BJP national vice president Ram Madhav on Tuesday, in a direct dig at LOP in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and his ally NC leadership, alleged that contrary to Congress’ accusations (against BJP), it was “former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi joined by the then Chief Minister Dr Farooq Abdullah, who had massively rigged assembly elections in 1987, leading to emergence of terrorism in J&K.” Referring to the Congress’ allegations against the Modi government of “committing electoral frauds”, Madhav asserted, “In fact, in the history of the country, only two Prime Ministers actually committed such proven electoral frauds. One was Rahulji’s grand-mother Indira Gandhi, whose election was declared “void” by Allahabad court proving the charge that the official election machinery was misused by her to emerge victorious. In response, Indira imposed an emergency in the country.” “Secondly in 1987 in J&K assembly elections, Rahul’s father and the then Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi in league with Farooq Abdullah, who was then J&K Chief Minister had resorted to large-scale irregularities in the election process, leading to emergence of terrorism here (in J&K). These are well-recorded facts,” he maintained. Madhav, accompanied by J&K BJP general secretaries Gopal Mahajan, Baldev Singh Billawaria, chief spokesperson Sunil Sethi and other senior leaders, was addressing a press conference at BJP headquarter, Trikuta Nagar, Jammu. He accused the Congress of attempting to fulfill its avowed objective of “regime change” through “anarchy, violence and riots as it could not win power through democratic means of electoral battle.” “But people are with Modiji and this became evident again during their opposition’s much hyped Ramlila Maidan rally, where 23 parties together could hardly bring 50,000 or 60,000 people against their haughty claims of 1 million people. BJP, even in a normal rally in an assembly constituency of Jammu, can bring 5000 people,” he maintained. With regard to questions about NC rebellion post cabinet expansion and speculations linking his visit to efforts of BJP government formation, he refused to make any comment. “I’m here to address only the issue related to fake propaganda being run by the opposition on Special Intensive Revision (SIR) across the country and particularly in the union capital. For the past few months, the main opposition party Congress and its leader Rahul Gandhi have been busy spreading lies that the Election Commission has manipulated the country's electoral system,” Madhav said. “The Election Commission will reply to these allegations and they have already submitted a detailed affidavit in the Supreme Court vis-a-vis entire process of SIR and all facts related to it. But we want to expose Congress’ real intentions behind the controversy they wilfully created to achieve its objective of “regime-change” but not through democratic means. Their leaders are spelling out openly at every public forum and social media that they wanted regime-change like it happened in Bangladesh and Nepal,” he said. It was because the opposition had realised that they could not defeat BJP, the Prime Minister Narenda Modi electorally, so they (Congress and other opposition parties) wanted to overthrow democratically-elected regime and wrest power through anarchy, creating doubts about constitutional institutions, Madhav alleged. “However, the people of India will never allow the Congress to succeed in its intentions to spread anarchy in the country,” he asserted. Madhav described all allegations of Congress regarding SIR exercise, presently underway in many parts of the country and already completed in several states, as “out and out white lies.” BJP national vice president reiterated that the Election Commission, through constitutional exercise SIR, was actually cleansing the electoral system of “all sins of Congress which fiddled with the electoral rolls during the past several decades.” He asserted that the Congress's politics of confusion, confrontation and institutional distrust would not succeed in India. Madhav stated the SIR exercise, being undertaken after nearly two decades, was a legitimate democratic process in which Booth Level Officers (BLOs) were conducting door-to-door verification to ensure the accuracy and integrity of electoral rolls and identify illegal entries, including those of foreign nationals residing illegally in India. He alleged that the Congress wanted illegal voters to remain on electoral rolls because its political calculations depended on manipulating the electoral environment. He said the opposition's repeated allegations against constitutional institutions were part of a larger conspiracy to create street unrest and engineer political instability, drawing parallels with developments in neighbouring Bangladesh and Nepal. Regarding Congress’ main allegation that the names of 13 crore voters were deleted (through SIR exercise), Madhav questioned why it could not bring those people to the fore. “Where are those 13 Cr voters whose names, according to the Congress, have been deleted? SIR is cleansing electoral rolls of discrepancies through constitutionally valid SIR exercise, happening after a gap of 20 years. The names of dead (around 2-3 Cr), transferred (around 6 Cr), non-existent voters (1 or 2 Cr) and infiltrators who are illegal voters have been deleted and are being deleted. Like in Jammu, Rohingyas have settled at many places. The names of such infiltrators, illegal immigrants get deleted. This is imperative. Does the Congress want those infiltrators to be included in the electoral rolls as its prospective voters,” he threw a poser. He asserted that one to two crore people, who were genuine voters yet their names were deleted through computer based mechanism, could go and get their names included in the electoral rolls as per the set procedure and there was no bar on it. He alleged that earlier Congress was blaming EVMs for its defeats but could not establish the charge and currently, it was accusing BJP of stealing mandate through “vote-Chori.” “Between 2014 and 2024, the Congress lost 56 assembly polls and three parliamentary elections i.e., 2014, 2019 and 2024. But that time present Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar was not there. Then how was Congress defeated? They (Congress) have no logic and it is resorting to political conspiracy. The government is willing to convene a special Parliament session but they (opposition) are running away. They are only trying to provoke people through false propaganda,” Madhav alleged. He mocked that the Congress was crediting BJP for its electoral victories in Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana stating that they were made to win by it (BJP) so that it (BJP) could “justify its electoral fraud in other states and parliamentary polls.” “Nothing could be more ridiculous than this illogical explanation about their wins through the same electoral system, which they are criticising. This depicts how pitiable their condition is,” he said. Madhav explained that they (Congress) were seeking replacement of EVMs with the ballot papers. In the recent municipal polls conducted through ballot papers in October, Congress could win only two wards out of 42 wards. In MLC elections, which are always conducted through ballot papers, out of 28 seats, BJP-allies won 16 seats and BJP won 13 seats but Congress could win only one seat. Responding to another question, he said that there could be possibilities of some discrepancies or errors in SIR exercise, conducted through computer-based mechanisms. “Those errors can always be rectified. If the names of genuine voters get deleted, they can get their names added in the voter lists through relevant forms. Revision is a constitutional process. In Uttarakhand, where I’m (BJP) Prabhari, names deleted mainly comprised Hindu voters and this happened at some other places. Eligible persons can always get their names included,” he explained.

opening: Jammu, Nov 3: BJP national vice president Ram Madhav on Tuesday, in a direct dig at LOP in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and his ally NC leadership, alleged that contrary to Congress’ accusations (against BJP), it was “former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi joined by the then Chief Minister Dr Farooq Abdullah, who had massively rigged assembly elections in 1987, leading to emergence of terrorism in J&K.” Referring to the Congress’ allegations against the Modi government of “committing electoral frauds”, Madhav asserted, “In fact, in the history of the country, only two Prime Ministers actually committed such proven electoral frauds.
One was Rahulji’s grand-mother Indira Gandhi, whose election was declared “void” by Allahabad court proving the charge that the official election machinery was misused by her to emerge victorious.
body: In response, Indira imposed an emergency in the country.” “Secondly in 1987 in J&K assembly elections, Rahul’s father and the then Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi in league with Farooq Abdullah, who was then J&K Chief Minister had resorted to large-scale irregularities in the election process, leading to emergence of terrorism here (in J&K).
These are well-recorded facts,” he maintained.

Madhav, accompanied by J&K BJP general secretaries Gopal Mahajan, Baldev Singh Billawaria, chief spokesperson Sunil Sethi and other senior leaders, was addressing a press conference at BJP headquarter, Trikuta Nagar, Jammu.

He accused the Congress of attempting to fulfill its avowed objective of “regime change” through “anarchy, violence and riots as it could not win power through democratic means of electoral battle.” “But people are with Modiji and this became evident again during their opposition’s much hyped Ramlila Maidan rally, where 23 parties together could hardly bring 50,000 or 60,000 people against their haughty claims of 1 million people.
With regard to questions about NC rebellion post cabinet expansion and speculations linking his visit to efforts of BJP government formation, he refused to make any comment.
“I’m here to address only the issue related to fake propaganda being run by the opposition on Special Intensive Revision (SIR) across the country and particularly in the union capital.

For the past few months, the main opposition party Congress and its leader Rahul Gandhi have been busy spreading lies that the Election Commission has manipulated the country's electoral system,” Madhav said.
“The Election Commission will reply to these allegations and they have already submitted a detailed affidavit in the Supreme Court vis-a-vis entire process of SIR and all facts related to it.
But we want to expose Congress’ real intentions behind the controversy they wilfully created to achieve its objective of “regime-change” but not through democratic means.
Their leaders are spelling out openly at every public forum and social media that they wanted regime-change like it happened in Bangladesh and Nepal,” he said.

It was because the opposition had realised that they could not defeat BJP, the Prime Minister Narenda Modi electorally, so they (Congress and other opposition parties) wanted to overthrow democratically-elected regime and wrest power through anarchy, creating doubts about constitutional institutions, Madhav alleged.
“However, the people of India will never allow the Congress to succeed in its intentions to spread anarchy in the country,” he asserted.

Madhav described all allegations of Congress regarding SIR exercise, presently underway in many parts of the country and already completed in several states, as “out and out white lies.” BJP national vice president reiterated that the Election Commission, through constitutional exercise SIR, was actually cleansing the electoral system of “all sins of Congress which fiddled with the electoral rolls during the past several decades.” He asserted that the Congress's politics of confusion, confrontation and institutional distrust would not succeed in India.
Madhav stated the SIR exercise, being undertaken after nearly two decades, was a legitimate democratic process in which Booth Level.

Officers (BLOs) were conducting door-to-door verification to ensure the accuracy and integrity of electoral rolls and identify illegal entries, including those of foreign nationals residing illegally in India.
He alleged that the Congress wanted illegal voters to remain on electoral rolls because its political calculations depended on manipulating the electoral environment.

He said the opposition's repeated allegations against constitutional institutions were part of a larger conspiracy to create street unrest and engineer political instability, drawing parallels with developments in neighbouring Bangladesh and Nepal.
Regarding Congress’ main allegation that the names of 13 crore voters were deleted (through SIR exercise), Madhav questioned why it could not bring those people to the fore.
“Where are those 13 Cr voters whose names, according to the Congress, have been deleted?
SIR is cleansing electoral rolls of discrepancies through constitutionally valid SIR exercise, happening after a gap of 20 years.
The names of dead (around 2-3 Cr), transferred (around 6 Cr), non-existent voters (1 or 2 Cr) and infiltrators who are illegal voters have been deleted and are being deleted.
Like in Jammu, Rohingyas have settled at many places.
The names of such infiltrators, illegal immigrants get deleted.
This is imperative.
Does the Congress want those infiltrators to be included in the electoral rolls as its prospective voters,” he threw a poser.

He asserted that one to two crore people, who were genuine voters yet their names were deleted through computer based mechanism, could go and get their names included in the electoral rolls as per the set procedure and there was no bar on it.

He alleged that earlier Congress was blaming EVMs for its defeats but could not establish the charge and currently, it was accusing BJP of stealing mandate through “vote-Chori.” “Between 2014 and 2024, the Congress lost 56 assembly polls and three parliamentary elections i.e., 2014, 2019 and 2024.
But that time present Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar was not there.
Then how was Congress defeated?
They (Congress) have no logic and it is resorting to political conspiracy.
The government is willing to convene a special Parliament session but they (opposition) are running away.
They are only trying to provoke people through false propaganda,” Madhav alleged.

He mocked that the Congress was crediting BJP for its electoral victories in Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana stating that they were made to win by it (BJP) so that it (BJP) could “justify its electoral fraud in other states and parliamentary polls.” “Nothing could be more ridiculous than this illogical explanation about their wins through the same electoral system, which they are criticising.
This depicts how pitiable their condition is,” he said.
Madhav explained that they (Congress) were seeking replacement of EVMs with the ballot papers.
In the recent municipal polls conducted through ballot papers in October, Congress could win only two wards out of 42 wards.
In MLC elections, which are always conducted through ballot papers, out of 28 seats, BJP-allies won 16 seats and BJP won 13 seats but Congress could win only one seat.
Responding to another question, he said that there could be possibilities of some discrepancies or errors in SIR exercise, conducted through computer-based mechanisms.
“Those errors can always be rectified.
If the names of genuine voters get deleted, they can get their names added in the voter lists through relevant forms.
Revision is a constitutional process.
In Uttarakhand, where I’m (BJP) Prabhari, names deleted mainly comprised Hindu voters and this happened at some other places.
Eligible persons can always get their names included,” he explained.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Asserts Right to Protest Must Not Lead to Indefinite Occupation of Public Spaces
stories.title: Supreme Court Asserts Right to Protest Must Not Lead to Indefinite Occupation of Public Spaces
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: New Delhi, Nov 3: The Supreme Court on Tuesday orally observed that the right to protest cannot be exercised by occupying a designated protest site indefinitely, stressing that such places must be allotted for specified periods to ensure that other groups also get an opportunity to exercise their constitutional rights.

A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana made the observations while hearing a batch of petitions arising from the October protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.
"You cannot occupy a site for all time to come.
There are other protesters.
Where will the farmers go?
Where will the workers go?
Where will the trade unions go?
Where will the homeless go?
Everybody has a right to protest," the apex court remarked.

It further observed that protest sites must be made available to different groups for designated periods, adding that no organisation could claim an exclusive right over a public space merely because it had occupied it first.
"There may be one site or two, but everybody has a right to protest.
You cannot exclude other people merely because you have occupied the site," the CJI-led Bench said.

stories.headline: Supreme Court freezes November salary of BMC chief Ashwini Bhide for failing to remove encroachments
stories.title: Supreme Court freezes November salary of BMC chief Ashwini Bhide for failing to remove encroachments
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: THE SUPREME Court on Tuesday issued notice to BMC Commissioner Ashwini Bhide, asking her to show cause why it should not initiate contempt of court proceedings against her for failing to comply with its direction to clear encroachments from land intended for a bus station project in Borivalli, and ordered suspension of her salary for the month of November.

A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana turned down the BMC’s request for 30 more days to execute the direction of removing encroachments and imposed a penalty of Rs 5 lakh on the municipal body.
The SC bench noted that its earlier directions were yet to be acted upon and wondered if there was any collusion between the officials and encroachers.

The CJI said, “This is an absolutely mischievous breach of the directions of the Supreme Court, with the direct connivance and support of the encroachers.” He warned that the court can put it all down in the order if the officials do not mend their ways.
Justice Bagchi told the BMC counsel, “You will not be drawing a salary till the 1st of December 2026.
So comply before that.
You come here and then you can draw your salary.”
Dismissing the BMC’s prayer for further extension of time, the CJI said: “Let them sit in the midnight and pass the orders.
Let them know how to work.”
The contempt application was moved by the project proponent, who alleged that the municipal authorities had failed to clear the encroachments.

Hearing the case on November 13 last year, the SC had said that “as regard to the removal of unauthorised encroachments, prima facie, we find that the municipal authorities are attempting to wriggle out of their previous stand and responsibility.” However, before initiating contempt proceedings, it granted one opportunity to the Commissioner “to file” a “personal affidavit along with (i) the names and particulars of the occupants; (ii) the copies of the notices issued to them; (iii) the copies of their reply, if any, received pursuant to such notices; (iv) the documents relied upon by the occupants in support of their plea of tenancy or ownership, if any; and (v) any enquiry/exercise undertaken by the Municipal Authorities to verify the genuineness of such documents.”

While hearing it again on July 28, 2026, the BMC said although notices against the encroachers were issued under the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966, most of them dragged the corporation into litigation before the civil court.
